claims.claim: A dental crown in the US typically costs on the order of $700-$1,400 (national average range), consistent with the digest's $800-$1,500 band.
claims.episode_span: a delivered fee that commonly ranges from two hundred to five hundred dollars for the filling and eight hundred to fifteen hundred for the crown
claims.source_title: How Much Do Dental Crowns Cost? Pricing and Insurance Guide - CareCredit
claims.supporting_quote: The national average cost* of a dental crown can range from $697 to $1,399. The price you pay for dental crowns is impacted by the type of dental crown you receive.

claims.claim: A composite dental filling averages about $226 in the US, ranging roughly $173-$439, consistent with the digest's $200-$500 band.
claims.episode_span: a delivered fee that commonly ranges from two hundred to five hundred dollars for the filling and eight hundred to fifteen hundred for the crown
claims.source_title: How Much Do Dental Fillings Cost? Pricing and Procedure Guide - CareCredit
claims.supporting_quote: The national average cost* of a composite filling is $226, but the cost ranges between $173 and $439, depending upon the tooth that is being filled and the depth of the cavity, as well as insurance coverage.

claims.claim: More than 50 countries allow dental therapists to provide some dental services (13 US states), supporting the claim that several jurisdictions already allow task-shifting.
claims.episode_span: shifting routine preventive and simple restorative tasks to hygienists and therapists operating under clearer protocols, which several jurisdictions already allow at pilot scale
claims.supporting_quote: More than 50 countries allow dental therapists to provide some dental services.

claims.claim: Research indicates dental therapists expand access to dental care without undermining quality, supporting the safe-transfer-of-tasks premise.
claims.episode_span: any safe transfer of tasks to less specialized operators immediately changes the arithmetic of the entire service
claims.supporting_quote: dental therapists provide greater access to dental care without undermining the quality of care

claims.claim: Becoming a dentist requires four years of dental education at an accredited dental school (after pre-dental college work), with additional years for specialties.
claims.episode_span: each visit consuming chair time from a clinician whose training spans four years of dental school plus residency
claims.source_title: Dentist - South Florida District Dental Association
claims.supporting_quote: Requirements include a high school diploma, three or four years of pre-dental courses at an accredited college or university and four years of dental education at an accredited dental school.
